extracted.intended_audience: NIH peer reviewers of institutional T32 training grant applications (and applicants seeking to understand review criteria)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for peer review of institutional T32 training grant applications, specifying scored review criteria and additional requirements reviewers should evaluate when determining overall impact/priority scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring Scale
rubrics_metrics.description: Each of the review criteria receives an individual score of 1 to 9 (1=outstanding, to 9=poor). An overall impact/priority score is determined by considering the scored criteria, plus additional review criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individual criterion scores (1–9) feed into an overall impact/priority score; reviewers should weigh the seven major scored criteria along with additional review criteria when determining overall impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training Program
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate the goals and objectives of the training program, the training program structure (didactic, research, professional development), duration and intensity, specific cohort sizes and characteristics, and coordination among program components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess clarity and appropriateness of goals/objectives, balance of didactic and research components, adequacy of duration/intensity for trainee development, justification of cohort sizes, and how program components coordinate to achieve training aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training Program Director/Principal Investigator (PD/PI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate PD/PI leadership experience in training, time commitment, research expertise, track record of mentorship, and vision for the program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the PD/PI has demonstrated leadership and prior success in training, sufficient protected time to lead the program, relevant research credentials, a documented mentorship record, and a clear, realistic programmatic vision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preceptors/Mentors
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the quality and experience of mentors, their funding levels (active grants supporting trainees), diversity of expertise, track record of training successful trainees, and time commitment to training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should judge whether mentors provide appropriate scientific and career guidance, have adequate current funding to support trainee projects, represent complementary expertise, have evidence of trainee success, and can commit time to mentorship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Past Training Record
rubrics_metrics.description: Review how successful the program has been in attracting and retaining individuals from diverse populations; how successful trainees are in completing the program; trainee productivity in research accomplishments and publications; success in obtaining further training appointments, fellowships, and career development awards; and achievement of productive scientific careers (research grants, honors, high-impact publications, scientific leadership).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine program outcome data (e.g., trainee completion rates, publications, subsequent awards and positions), evidence of long-term career success of alumni, and effectiveness at recruiting/retaining diverse trainees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional Training Environment, Commitment, and Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess quality of facilities, institutional commitment (financial, in-kind), coordination with other training programs, trainee support services, and mentorship infrastructure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether institutional resources and commitments are sufficient and clearly documented, whether facilities and support services facilitate trainee development, and how the program leverages or coordinates with other institutional training efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trainee Recruitment, Selection, and Retention Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate plans for diversity recruitment (URM, persons with disabilities, women), selection criteria, application/admission process, and retention strategies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should look for specific, evidence-based recruitment strategies, clear selection criteria and processes, and concrete retention plans to support trainees through program completion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short-Term and Research Training Positions (where applicable)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess justification for short-term experiences and the quality of summer/intensive programs when such positions are part of the training grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When applicable, evaluate the rationale for short-term training slots, expected training benefit, oversight/mentorship for short-term trainees, and the design/quality of summer or intensive training offerings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan for Instruction in the Responsible Conduct of Research (RCR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate the plan's format, subject matter, faculty participation, frequency, and plan for evaluation of trainees' RCR understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the RCR plan is appropriate in content and delivery, includes active faculty involvement, occurs at a suitable frequency, and has a credible method for evaluating trainee understanding and integration of RCR principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan for Instruction in Methods for Enhancing Reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Required for biomedical training programs; evaluate coverage of rigorous research design and methods for enhancing reproducibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should determine whether the training adequately addresses rigorous experimental design, statistical practices, transparency, and other methods that promote reproducible research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recruitment and Retention Plan to Enhance Diversity
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess specific strategies, goals and metrics, and the evaluation plan to enhance diversity among trainees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for measurable goals, clear strategies targeted to underrepresented groups, and an evaluation framework to track progress and effectiveness of diversity initiatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Special Populations (where applicable)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider inclusion plans and considerations for special populations such as children, older adults, and sex/gender considerations where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When relevant, evaluate whether the program addresses ethical and methodological issues for special populations and has appropriate plans for inclusion or justification for exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application Materials / Required Documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Required application materials include the Training Program Plan; Tables (Table 1: Census; Table 2: Participating Faculty; Tables 3–8: Trainee outcomes; etc.); letters of support from key institutional officials; PD/PI and key personnel biosketches; and detailed budget and justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should confirm completeness and appropriateness of required documents and tables, adequacy of institutional letters of support, appropriateness of personnel qualifications in biosketches, and justification of budget requests as they relate to program aims.
